html:
The Sanpoil are an Interior Salish people of north-central Washington, living along the Sanpoil River and the Columbia River. They are one of the twelve bands of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation.

They were salmon people, fishing the runs of the Columbia and its tributaries, and they were known among anthropologists for a strongly peaceful way of life, with little war and leaders chosen by consent. In the 1870s their land became part of the Colville Reservation. In the early 1940s the Grand Coulee Dam closed the Columbia to salmon above it and flooded their river villages and fishing places. Their neighbours included the Sinixt and the Spokane.
sum: The Sanpoil are an Interior Salish people of north-central Washington, living along the Sanpoil River and the Columbia River. They are one of the twelve bands of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation.
